name: studio
description: A project desk for non-code work — writing, content, and small-business projects. studio:new-project scaffolds a consistent folder skeleton and interviews you for the brief (audience, tone, voice, goals, and what one finished piece looks like); studio:name gives a project a working name in minutes (a codename kept out of permanent places like store identifiers and legal pages), brainstorms name ideas with you when you just want to riff (metaphor territories and candidates, shown openly, no checks), and, when launch is near, runs a real naming round — brief, metaphor territories, filtered candidates, live availability checks for domains, GitHub, App Store and Google Play plus trademark and handle links, a scored shortlist with origin stories, and a written record; studio:scope shapes a fast first version (MVP) the way release-shaping does but without the code machinery — fix the time budget (appetite), name the risky unknowns (rabbit holes), and triage every item include/defer/split/risk-first into v1 or later versions; studio:next-piece develops the next deliverable end to end, adapted to the project's format (a script, a chapter, a tour, an issue — not assumed to be a podcast episode); studio:project-desk runs the day-to-day (what's due this week, the publishing calendar, and a plain-language decision log). Same structure every project, so you always know where the plan, the decisions, and the work live.
